events.title: Economy Grows 5.6% in H1 2026; BCP Raises 2026 GDP Forecast to 4.5% (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Paraguay's Monthly Economic Activity Indicator (IMAEP) grew 5.6% year-on-year in June and accumulated 5.6% in H1 2026, driven by the primary sector (+9.8%), secondary (+4.7%) and services (+5.1%). The BCP raised its 2026 GDP growth projection from 4.2% to 4.5% and cut its inflation forecast to 3.3%, citing stronger-than-expected activity across agriculture, manufacturing, utilities and services.

events.title: Exports Surge 25.2% to USD 12.13B, Reversing Trade Deficit to USD 679M Surplus (2026-08-13)
events.summary: Paraguay's exports reached USD 12,133.7 million in January-July 2026 (+25.2% year-on-year), while imports grew 12.8% to USD 11,454.6 million, producing a USD 679.1 million trade surplus — a sharp reversal from the USD 462.9 million deficit a year earlier. Soybeans led the expansion at USD 2,648.6 million (+49%), followed by maquila exports (+32.1%) and industrial manufactures (+35%).

events.title: Dollar Rebounds Above G. 6,000; Forward Contracts Grow 22.8% as BCP Urges Hedging (2026-08-14)
events.summary: After breaking below G. 6,000 for the first time since 2018 (low of G. 5,944.39 on August 1), the US dollar rebounded to G. 6,027 (BCP reference rate, August 14), a mild correction within an overall appreciating-guaraní trend. The BCP reported forward contracts grew 22.8% year-on-year, highlighting hedging instruments as essential amid exchange-rate volatility that has seen the guaraní appreciate roughly 25% over ten months.

events.title: Three Years of Peña: Poverty Down to 16%, Unemployment 3.6%, 242,000 New Jobs (2026-08-14)
events.summary: On the eve of President Santiago Peña's third anniversary (August 15), the government reported monetary poverty fell from 21.6% (2023) to 16% (2025), unemployment dropped from 4.5% to 3.6%, and 242,000 new jobs were created. However, critics argue the growth 'does not reach everyone', citing the persistent IPS crisis, precarious labor and rural exclusion.

events.title: Peña Unveils Energy Reform: Ministry of Mines and Energy + Independent Electricity Regulator (2026-08-13)
events.summary: President Peña presented two draft bills opening a 15-day public consultation: creation of a Ministry of Mines and Energy (elevating the sector from its current vice-ministry status under MOPC) and an independent electricity regulator. The reform responds to surging demand — private companies have formally requested 15,000 MW, equal to Itaipú's entire capacity, and the sector needs an estimated USD 11 billion over 13-15 years.

events.title: Investor Pass Grants Direct Permanent Residency via Investment (2026-08-04)
events.summary: Through Resolution 0283/2026, Paraguay launched the 'Investor Pass', granting direct permanent residency via the Foreign Investor Certificate (CIE) with four investment routes: industrial/manufacturing from USD 70,000, real estate from USD 200,000, financial instruments from USD 200,000, and tourism from USD 150,000. The program cuts dividend tax for residents from 15% to 8% and is largely digital, with the CIE issued in five business days.

events.title: Experts Endorse New Energy Ministry but Demand ANDE Functions Be Protected (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Energy specialists broadly backed the proposed Ministry of Energy and electricity regulator but warned the new entity must not strip functions from ANDE, whose organic charter should be updated without weakening it. The debate unfolded amid a Sitrande union complaint alleging favoritism toward the company Atome in tariff policy, underscoring governance sensitivities in the reform.

events.title: 'Paraguay duele' Protests and Cacerolazo on Eve of Peña's Third Anniversary (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Unions and peasant organizations (Corriente Clasista y Combativa, OTEP, the IPS union, Federación Nacional Campesina) marched in Asunción under the slogan 'Paraguay duele' (Paraguay hurts), a rebuttal to Peña's 'Vamos a estar mejor' campaign. A cacerolazo near Mburuvicha Róga was blocked by a heavy police cordon. Demonstrators denounced deteriorating labor, health and social-security conditions and the criminalization of protest.

events.title: Three Years of Government: Strong Macro Numbers 'Don't Reach Everyone' (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Despite GDP growth of 6.6% in 2025 (the region's highest), Última Hora reports that prosperity is unevenly distributed. Protest leaders highlighted the IPS crisis — medicine shortages, lack of beds, over 11,000 precarious contractors including nurses earning below the minimum wage — and the concentration of land with evictions of peasant and indigenous communities, framing the disconnect between headline growth and lived conditions.

events.title: Rural Youth Migration Rises as 'There Are No Jobs in the Countryside or City' (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Peasant and youth leaders responding to the government's third anniversary said thousands of young people are migrating from the countryside to Asunción, Brazil and Spain due to lack of employment and opportunities. They cited shortages of work, housing and land, and precarious conditions for teachers, as growth concentrated in agribusiness fails to generate rural jobs.

events.title: Paraguay Reaffirms Openness to China Trade Without Breaking Taiwan Ties (2026-08-11)
events.summary: During the 7th China-Mercosur dialogue, Paraguay reiterated it is open to trade with mainland China 'as long as there are no conditions' regarding its diplomatic ties with Taiwan. Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez previously stated Paraguay 'has no restrictions' under those terms. Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole ally in South America and the only Mercosur member without diplomatic relations with China.

events.title: China Rejects Paraguay's 'Wishful Thinking' on Two-Track Trade (2026-08-12)
events.summary: Chinese officials and experts rejected Paraguay's bid to trade with China while maintaining ties with Taiwan as 'wishful thinking', insisting that economic cooperation cannot be separated from the One-China principle. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun urged Paraguay to 'stand on the right side of history'. China remains Paraguay's largest supplier of goods (phones, computers, tires) despite the absence of diplomatic relations.

events.title: Mercosur-Japan EPA Talks Advance as Japan Names Chief Negotiator (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Japan appointed Hayashi Teiji, former ambassador to Brazil and TPP negotiator, as chief negotiator for the Mercosur-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, with talks expected to begin in autumn 2026. The EPA, formally launched at the June 30 Mercosur summit in Asunción, would cover a market of roughly 400 million people and a combined GDP of about USD 7 trillion.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: Second 5G Auction Finalized: Tigo (2.3 GHz) and Personal (3.7 GHz) Commit to 750 Base Stations (2026-08-12)
events.summary: CONATEL finalized the second 5G auction: Tigo won 2.3-2.4 GHz (USD 1.6 million) and Personal won 3.7-3.8 GHz (USD 1 million). Operators have 90 days to submit technical deployment plans and 180 days to install the first base station; each must deploy at least 100 base stations within four years, with a combined commitment of USD 80 million and about 750 base stations in five years (5G NR Release 15 or higher).
events.client_tag: Tigo, Personal — 5G deployment, USD 80M combined, 750 base stations

events.title: Conatel Defends Nubicom, Confirms First Base Station Installed; Peña Links Criticism to China Pressure (2026-08-12)
events.summary: CONATEL denied reports of Nubicom's non-compliance, stating the Argentine ISP has installed its first base station and is conducting tests in Asunción, following its USD 200 million investment pledge. President Peña attributed criticism of the first 5G auction to alleged pressure from China, noting the tender required equipment from countries with diplomatic relations with Paraguay.
events.client_tag: Nubicom — 5G deployment, USD 200M pledge; regulatory defense

events.title: Datawaves Delivers Edge Data Center Modules to Claro Paraguay (2026-08-11)
events.summary: Argentine manufacturer Datawaves delivered modular edge data center units (including a modular FTTH module) to Claro Paraguay, adding to more than 25 modules supplied to América Móvil's Claro across Argentina and Paraguay, including four for Paraguay. The modules include cooling, seven racks and free cooling, supporting Claro's fiber and network expansion.
events.client_tag: Claro — edge data center / FTTH infrastructure

events.title: Tigo (Telecel): Wins 2.3 GHz 5G License for USD 1.6M; 100 Base Stations in Four Years (2026-08-12)
events.summary: Tigo (Telecel SAE, Millicom) won the 2.3-2.4 GHz band for USD 1.6 million in the second 5G auction. It must submit technical plans within 90 days, install its first base station within 180 days, and deploy at least 100 base stations within four years under the combined USD 80 million investment commitment.
events.client_tag: Millicom/Tigo — 5G 2.3 GHz deployment; network equipment, base stations

events.title: Personal (Núcleo): Wins 3.7 GHz 5G License for USD 1M (2026-08-12)
events.summary: Personal (Núcleo SA, Telecom Argentina) won the 3.7-3.8 GHz band for USD 1 million — the same prime band used by its Argentine parent. Personal leads Paraguay's FTTH market and is the second-largest mobile operator with 1.66 million users, positioning it to accelerate 5G in urban centers under the 180-day first-base-station deadline.
events.client_tag: Telecom Argentina/Personal — 5G 3.7 GHz deployment; FTTH, fiber

events.title: Claro (América Móvil): Datawaves Edge Modules Bolster Fiber and Data Infrastructure (2026-08-11)
events.summary: Claro Paraguay received modular edge data center units from Datawaves, expanding its fiber and network infrastructure. Claro, which activated the country's first 5G network in December 2025 with Nokia equipment and an initial USD 35 million investment, continues its expansion across Greater Asunción and key cities, serving 947,000 mobile users.
events.client_tag: América Móvil/Claro — edge data center, FTTH, 5G expansion

events.title: Nubicom: First 5G Base Station Confirmed, USD 200M Pledge Under Scrutiny (2026-08-12)
events.summary: Nubicom, the Argentine ISP that won 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band in the 2025 auction with a USD 200 million pledge, saw CONATEL confirm its first base station is installed with testing underway in Asunción, denying earlier non-compliance reports. The operator's progress is closely watched as a test of new-entrant viability in Paraguay's 5G market.

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.impact_analysis:
🟢 Macro Tailwind — Growth & Trade: Paraguay's economy expanded 5.6% in H1 2026, prompting the BCP to raise its 2026 GDP forecast to 4.5%, while January-July exports surged 25.2% to a USD 679 million surplus. For businesses, this signals robust domestic demand and improving external accounts. However, growth remains concentrated in agribusiness (soybeans +49%) and maquila (+32%), so telecom and digital-infrastructure vendors must align with a diversifying but still commodity-led economy.

🟡 FX Volatility — Hedging Urgency: After breaking below G. 6,000 (a 2018 low), the dollar rebounded to G. 6,027 by August 14, and BCP-reported forward contracts grew 22.8% as firms rushed to hedge. Importers of capital goods benefit from the strong guaraní, but any USD-revenue business faces margin risk. The BCP's neutral stance and the ~25% ten-month appreciation argue for proactive FX hedging across operations.

🟢 Energy Reform — Structural Opportunity: Peña's proposal to create a Ministry of Mines and Energy plus an independent regulator, backed by 15,000 MW of private demand requests and an estimated USD 11 billion investment need over 13-15 years, is the most consequential policy signal for the digital-energy sector. Data-center and AI operators (HIVE, the Taiwan hub) stand to gain from clearer rules and tariff predictability, though ANDE's role must be carefully delineated.

🟡 Regulatory & Social Friction: The 'Paraguay duele' protests and cacerolazo on the eve of Peña's third anniversary, plus the unresolved IPS crisis (11,000+ precarious workers), signal rising social discontent despite strong macro numbers. The 5G rollout remains on track, but CONATEL's handling of Nubicom — and Peña's framing of criticism as Chinese pressure — adds political noise to a sector already navigating trusted-vendor restrictions that exclude Huawei and ZTE.

🔴 Concentration Risk — Client Exposure: All four licensed 5G operators (Claro, Nubicom, Tigo, Personal) now face deployment deadlines (180 days for the first base station, 100 base stations in four years), creating near-term equipment demand. But with the market consolidating around three foreign-controlled groups, suppliers face concentrated counterparty risk and should diversify across operators and into enterprise/private-network segments.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis:
🔴 High Risk — Diplomatic Constraints Persist: Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole South American ally, and the 7th China-Mercosur dialogue in August did not shift this. China's Foreign Ministry and state media explicitly rejected Paraguay's 'trade without breaking Taiwan ties' stance as 'wishful thinking', reaffirming the One-China principle as a precondition. Chinese enterprises should expect continued exclusion from public 5G tenders (Huawei and ZTE are barred under trusted-vendor clauses) and conduct rigorous compliance reviews before any Paraguay-linked engagement.

🟡 Medium Risk — Indirect Access Only: China is Paraguay's largest goods supplier (phones, computers, tires), and Chinese firms can still serve the market indirectly via Brazilian, Argentine or Chilean subsidiaries or trading intermediaries. The Mercosur-Japan EPA and the China-Mercosur dialogue open regional channels, but direct Chinese-branded infrastructure deals in sensitive sectors (telecom, energy) remain politically constrained.

🟢 Opportunity — Energy & Digital Infrastructure: The energy reform (Ministry of Mines and Energy, independent regulator) and the USD 11 billion investment need create demand for power equipment, transmission and grid modernization where Chinese suppliers (transformers, HVDC, renewables) can participate through consortiums with non-Chinese partners. Data-center growth (HIVE's 100 MW expansion, the Taiwan AI hub's up-to-1-GW roadmap) similarly requires massive electrical and cooling infrastructure.

🟢 Opportunity — Equipment via Third Parties: The 5G buildout (750 base stations, USD 80 million combined commitment) requires radios, fiber and edge infrastructure. Chinese equipment vendors, though barred from the public auction, can pursue enterprise/private networks, wholesale fiber, and partnerships with Latin American integrators (e.g., Datawaves-style module suppliers) that already serve Claro, Tigo and Personal.

🟡 Caution — Labor & Social Risk: Rising social discontent ('Paraguay duele' protests), the IPS crisis and rural youth migration point to labor-market friction despite headline growth. Chinese firms with field operations should review security and labor compliance, account for the PYG 3,044,000 minimum wage (+5% from July 2026) and the 16.5% IPS employer contribution, and monitor strike risk (the doctors' strike remains scheduled for August 24-28).
